title: PaQit: Energy-Runtime-Fidelity Co-Optimization for Neutral Atom Quantum Computers
abstract: Neutral-atom quantum computers provide a scalable platform for large-scale quantum computation due to their all-optical control, room-temperature operation, and flexible lattice geometry. Although the favorable energy characteristics of these systems are well recognized, the relationship between system-level energy consumption, runtime, and computational fidelity remains poorly understood, limiting practical scheduling decisions. In this work, we develop a hardware-grounded analytical model that captures how energy and runtime scale with qubit utilization in neutral-atom systems.   We introduce PaQit, a fidelity-aware qubit packing framework that integrates device-level Rydberg interaction physics with system-level scheduling to jointly optimize energy, runtime, and fidelity. By translating fidelity targets into packing decisions, PaQit identifies operating regimes that maximize parallelism while respecting interaction-driven crosstalk constraints. We validate the analytical framework using simulations of QuEra's analog Aquila system and digital Gemini system, as well as real hardware executions, demonstrating close agreement between the predicted trends and observed system behavior.
summary: The paper introduces PaQit, a novel framework designed to co-optimize energy, runtime, and fidelity in neutral-atom quantum computers. It models the critical trade-off where increasing qubit density boosts speed but degrades computation accuracy due to Rydberg interactions. By integrating device physics into scheduling decisions, PaQit provides actionable guidelines for operating these complex quantum hardware systems.
main_problem: The relationship between energy consumption, runtime, and computational fidelity in neutral-atom quantum computers is poorly understood, hindering practical scheduling decisions.
main_result: PaQit provides a framework that jointly optimizes these three metrics by translating target fidelity into specific qubit packing decisions based on Rydberg interaction physics.
method: The authors developed a hardware-grounded analytical model and a fidelity-aware qubit packing framework to guide system scheduling.
model_or_system: The platform is neutral-atom quantum computing using atoms trapped in optical lattices, where interactions are dominated by the $1/r_{ij}^6$ Rydberg blockade potential. The dynamics are modeled via a time-dependent Hamiltonian incorporating this interaction term.
key_observables: Energy consumption (P), Runtime (T), Computational Fidelity ($\mathcal{F}$), and Qubit Packing Density ($\eta$).
important_parameters: Static baseline power ($P_0$), Rydberg blockade radius ($r_b$), target fidelity ($f^*$), and packing efficiency ($\eta$).
main_assumptions: The system operates in a static-power-dominated regime where energy depends heavily on execution time, not just instantaneous utilization.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the bounds for serial versus maximally parallel execution. Figure 2 shows how PaQit determines optimal packing efficiency to minimize runtime and energy while meeting a target fidelity.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical limitations (Rydberg interactions) leading to trade-offs between density/throughput and fidelity, develops analytical models for power/time scaling under serial and parallel regimes, introduces PaQit to resolve this multi-objective optimization, and validates the framework using simulations of real hardware platforms.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the engineering constraints necessary for realizing large-scale quantum computation with neutral atoms by providing a quantitative link between physical interactions (Rydberg blockade) and system performance metrics (Energy/Time/Fidelity).
